responses.user_utterance: What’s the perfect length for a chain then? How do I know it’s correct for my bike?
responses.user_rubrik: What is the perfect length of a chain for a bike?
responses.text: There isn’t one “perfect” link count—chain length depends on your biggest chainring and largest rear cog. Use this simple sizing:  - Big–big method: Route the chain around the largest front ring and largest rear cog, bypassing the rear derailleur. Pull it tight, then add one full link (one inner + one outer). Cut there and install the quick link. For full-suspension frames, add one more link.  Quick checks after installing: - Big ring + biggest cog: Rear derailleur cage should be angled forward but not pulled dead-straight. - Small ring + smallest cog: Chain shouldn’t hang slack or let the cage fold under.  Notes: - Works for 1x and 2x/3x drivetrains. - Use a chain that matches your speed (e.g., 10/11/12‑speed) and respect directional arrows on some chains/quick links.  If you’re not set up with tools, a shop can size and fit a chain in minutes and confirm everything (limits, B‑tension) so it won’t drop.
